findings.evidence: The actual optimizer-group predicate was extracted from source and evaluated over 49 opaque parameter tokens with maximize=True and all tokens trainable. It returned True. No torch import or optimizer/model construction was used.
findings.minimal_change: Require group["maximize"] is False before model computation. Also require group["amsgrad"] is False if claiming the original default AdamW variant exactly.
findings.problem: An exact torch.optim.AdamW with all required parameters and declared lr/weight_decay/betas/eps passes when maximize=True. optimizer.step() then maximizes the focal CE. The helper claims unchanged original AdamW but never checks this group flag.
findings.title: Reject AdamW gradient ascent at the declared CE minimization boundary

findings.evidence: The actual optimizer predicate returned True for 49 unique group tokens with the three memory-token trainability flags false. The only requires_grad occurrence in the training helper is the gradient-list exclusion filter.
findings.minimal_change: Require all(p.requires_grad for p in model.parameters()) at this step boundary and check gradients over the complete parameter list. Keep all current group identity and finite/nonzero gradient checks.
findings.problem: The optimizer identity/count check still passes after a caller freezes memory or structural parameters. Constructor-time trainability does not protect later stage integration. The gradient list filters out requires_grad=False tensors, so its all-connected-gradient check cannot catch the omitted mechanism. Training can complete while the advertised all-weights-trainable final mechanism stays frozen.
findings.title: Enforce current trainability of every final-mechanism parameter
